pages.text: A salt dissolves until its ions' product reaches the $(thing)solubility product K_sp$(). Drive the water off a brine and its salts come out in order: in the $(item)Brine Evaporator$(), $(item)Gypsum$() at four times the strength, $(item)Halite$() at ten to twenty, and $(item)Lithium Carbonate$() from the bittern beyond thirty.
Set the pan temperature and the water driven off. Hotter is faster, but above about 335 K the crystals grow too fast and trap the other salts: the purity must stay above 80%.
